> [!IMPORTANT]
> **STATUS 2026-08-26: the design below is PARTIALLY SUPERSEDED. Do NOT implement from this body.**
> The Step 1 research pass measured two of its headline levers dead as stated: **chain FBBT as gate-fixer** (item 1: k ~ 2(n-1) gates stay ambiguous at the root on every capture, 175/176 on j003, vs the claimed k <= 6) and **the costate warm start as a feasible incumbent** (item 2: replays 0.08..12.29 blocks wall-infeasible on 7 captures). The k-gon dual simplex, pseudocosts, and the GCS/Lagrangian escalation are demoted; the disk kernel + arc chord cut + 3-way gate branch + round-and-simulate survive.
> **Start here instead:** the binding problem statement + staged implementation plan is in [this comment](https://github.com/Leg0shii/ParkourCalculatorMod/issues/422#issuecomment-5428709916); per-hypothesis verdicts with all numbers in `docs/research/global-solver-2026-08/ARCH2-STEP1-SIMPLIFY.md`. The outer stratfinder use case is split to #424 (parked).

## What and why

The current angle solver (ARCH-1) closes the byte-exact nonconvex gap with a stack of recovery heuristics
(degenerate-tick residual, sphere-decode snap, GateMip, BoundPrunedRecovery) layered on the convex SOCP
disk kernel. The STEP-9 OLD-vs-NEW benchmark (`docs/research/solver-rework-2026-08/BENCHMARK-STEP9.md`) shows
this works well on short / targeted momentum jumps (loopmm, j021, j345 all win) but degrades on the longest
runs: **j003 (n=176) lands a full block short of the optimum (-30.27 vs -31.30) and overruns its deadline**,
because the byte-exact *search* (not the SOCP, which is fast) does not scale to long gate-heavy tails.

A 3-agent SOTA survey (2026-08-25, full record in `docs/research/global-solver-2026-08/DESIGN.md`) found the
key structural fact: this is a **finite** mixed-integer problem (angles on the 65536-entry sine grid + binary
inertia gates), so a specialized branch-and-bound can return the **certified byte-exact global optimum**
(terminates at gap=0). That is something the current heuristic stack cannot guarantee, and something COPT (our
continuous-MISOCP oracle) does not give either (it certifies the continuous optimum, not the byte-exact one).

This issue **parks that research as the next-generation recovery ("ARCH-2")**. It is **DEFERRED**: first finish
the current ARCH-1 implementation (dead-code cleanup / STEP 7 + the j003 fix + in-game QA). ARCH-2 is the
strategic replacement for the recovery layer *after* ARCH-1 ships, not a blocker for it.

## The converged design (summary; full spec + formulas + references in DESIGN.md)

A reduced-space, FBBT-driven, certified spatial branch-and-bound. All three independent agents converged on it.

1. **Chain FBBT / per-axis reachability (biggest lever).** *[MEASURED DEAD as a gate-fixer, Step 1 H1; survives only as node arc tightening]* Forward+backward interval propagation along the
   linear velocity chain, O(n), to fixpoint. Because the gate threshold (5e-3 legacy / 9e-6 modern) is tiny
   vs player velocity, it FIXES almost every gate before branching; only k << n ambiguous ticks remain.
2. **O(n) costate warm start (a domain edge COPT lacks).** *[UNSOUND as incumbent source, Step 1 H3; demoted to node dive + tail pin + dual bound]* The closed-form adjoint of the 0.91 friction chain
   yields a Hamiltonian-optimal move sequence -> strong incumbent from tick 0. The terminal-linear objective's
   global coupling is fully captured by this one costate.
3. **Node relaxation = disk + walls + arc chord cut.** The exact convex hull of an angle-arc is the disk plus
   ONE linear half-plane `cos(mu)*x + sin(mu)*z >= m*cos(Delta)` -- a linear WALL that drops into the existing
   `DiskSocpKernel` with no change. IPM-at-nodes to start; swap to a k-gon LP + warm-started dual simplex for
   speed (the one hard build).
4. **Branch only the k ambiguous ticks** (2^n -> 2^k): arc bisection (feeds the chord cut) + 3-way gate split
   `w=0 / w in [eps,M] / w in [-M,-eps]` (no big-M).
5. **Round-and-simulate incumbents** through `ExactJumpModel`; finite domain => gap=0 gives the certified
   global optimum; the running gap maps onto the Fast/Optimize tiers.

## Why it can beat the status quo (honest)

- **Certified byte-exact global** (the heuristic stack has no optimality guarantee; COPT gives only the
  continuous optimum).
- **Domain edges COPT structurally lacks**: the closed-form costate warm start and exact per-axis LTI
  interval propagation that fixes most gate binaries.
- **Shippable pure Java 8** (COPT is native + licensed, unusable in the Forge loaders).

HONEST CAVEAT: the problem is NP-hard in the worst case (state-triggered gate; exact DP's value function has
exponentially many regions). The win is a large practical factor from reduced-space branching, not an
asymptotic one. If a run has many near-rest ticks (k grows with n), the edge erodes toward generic B&B --
**j003 is plausibly that worst case**. Mitigation: the receding-horizon window decomposition keeps per-window
k small; escalate the hardest runs to a tighter GCS/perspective relaxation or a temporal Lagrangian bound.

## Definition of done (binding, agreed 2026-08-26; replaces the deferred list below-style items)

100% done = every box below checked. Any session asked "what is left" answers by listing the unchecked boxes, verified with the stated checks. The original deferred list is superseded (k-gon engine demoted to build-on-measured-need; FBBT and costate roles changed per the Step 1 verdicts).

### G1 Strength: STRICTLY STRONGER than the released v1.9.0 AND v1.10.0 solvers

The two releases ship different solvers, so BOTH are baselines and dominance is measured against the better of the two per capture. Strictly-better-everywhere is impossible where a baseline already reaches the certified byte-exact optimum (equal is the ceiling there), so strength is encoded as: never worse than either, strictly better wherever improvement exists (judged against the certificate), strictly more captures solved, strictly faster.

- [ ] Baselines frozen from tags v1.9.0 (ac1b35e2) and v1.10.0 (08b013ad): worktree per tag, drop CorpusBench in (STEP-9 method), FAST + THOROUGH-10s over the full capture set including the new captures, committed as docs/research/solver-rework-2026-08/benchmark/corpus-REL190-{FAST,TH10}.tsv and corpus-REL1100-{FAST,TH10}.tsv. (The STEP-9 corpus-OLD TSVs are from 3d19c9ff, which is NEITHER release; do not reuse them as a release baseline.)
- [ ] Feasibility, strictly more: solves every capture either baseline solves (zero regressions vs the union of both), AND solves captures both baselines fail on, at minimum thousand-1-dup2 (deterministic), the two fixed-schedule knife-edge expects, and the currently-unsolved knife-edge hpk set from plan stage M1b.
- [ ] Objective, never worse and strictly better where possible: per capture, the shipped objective is >= max(v1.9.0, v1.10.0) within 1e-4 b; on every capture where that max sits more than 1e-4 b below the certified byte-exact optimum, strictly better than it; and wherever certification completes, equal to the certified optimum.
- [ ] Named precision targets green under -PslowTests: j003 at both tiers at the certified optimum (the -31.29 class, no deadline overrun); thousand-1-dup2 >= 6523.30772; fixed-schedule j1150 -2805.2990460856336 and j154 -1599.7237570.
- [ ] Determinism: 5 consecutive re-solves bit-identical on the multi-jump set (extends the OI-17 guard); no jitter class remains.
- [ ] Speed, strictly faster: FAST cold median, p90, and total wall-clock each strictly better than BOTH baselines' corresponding numbers on the same machine. This makes deleting the unconditional recovery floor mandatory (the released 1.10-era median is ~59 ms; the current cutover tree sits at ~107 ms), not optional polish.

### G2 Clean: no old or dead code

- [ ] The component inventory's DELETE column (posted as a comment in plan stage 1) is fully executed; zero subsumed recovery classes remain in core.
- [ ] Zero solver capability flags or system properties (check: grep -rn "pkc\." core/src/main, anglesolver hits are trace/debug logging only).
- [ ] Zero unreachable classes under core/.../anglesolver/ (check: jdeps reachability from AngleSolverEngine + the UI entry points, or the IDE unused-class inspection, clean).

### G3 Simple: ONE path

- [ ] Exactly one solve pipeline: FAST and OPTIMIZE run the same ordered stages and differ only in budget and termination, never in routing; no capture-conditional or edge-case solver branches (legacy vs modern physics constants live in ExactJumpModel only).
- [ ] Enforced by a committed test, not a one-time audit: a corpus-wide SolverTrace shape test asserting the set of distinct stage sequences across all captures at both tiers is exactly one (modulo loop counts and B&B depth).

### G4 OPTIMIZE contract

- [ ] OPTIMIZE returns its best incumbent plus a certified bound gap at the deadline on every corpus capture (the gap may be nonzero at budget; a hang or an empty return is a fail), and reaches gap = 0 on the small-capture certification set.

### G5 Ship hygiene

- [ ] Full slow suite green in CI; TESTS.md maps every new test class.
- [ ] In-game byte-exact QA (user-run): thousand, j003, one knife-edge capture, and the sphere-snap yaw-lock set, replayed through SimulatorEntity on 1.8.9 + Fabric.
- [ ] DESIGN.md status banner updated to point at the implemented state; #424 stays the only open follow-up; merged to dev and released via the normal train.

## Anything else

- Design record + build order + traps + full references: `docs/research/global-solver-2026-08/DESIGN.md`.
- Motivating benchmark + the j003 root-cause trace: `docs/research/solver-rework-2026-08/BENCHMARK-STEP9.md`
  and the STEP-9 BUILD-LOG entry.
- Key prior art / papers: Belotti et al. (Acta Numerica 2013, spatial B&B); Benson-Saglam (MISOCP survey);
  Coffrin-Hijazi-Van Hentenryck (QC / trig envelopes); Marcucci-Tedrake (perspective disjunctions, GCS);
  Bemporad-Borrelli-Morari (PWA value-function blow-up); Quirynen et al. (temporal binary fixing).
